content: Before taking ulipristal, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to progestins (such as levonorgestrel or norethindrone), or if you have any other allergies. This medication may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other complications. Ulipristal may cause dizziness, and consuming alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate this effect. Limit your intake of alcoholic beverages. This medication should not be used during pregnancy. It can pass into breast milk, and due to potential risks to the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended while using this drug. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Always keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some medications, such as griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), and others, may reduce the effectiveness of emergency birth control, potentially leading to pregnancy. If an overdose occurs, it is highly unlikely to cause severe symptoms. However, if someone experiences serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
